findings.title: 29 mutable-tag action references unpinned (checkout@v4 x18, dtolnay/rust-toolchain@v1 x12) while sibling actions are SHA-pinned
findings.description: actions/checkout@v4 and third-party dtolnay/rust-toolchain@v1 are referenced by mutable tags in all 6 workflows: ci.yml:53,64,86,96,127,149,164,221,252,279,317; security.yml:22-23,53-54; release.yml:68,71,136; docker.yml:17; pages.yml:32,35; bufflings.yml:21-22. In the same files, cargo-deny (ci.yml:54), rust-cache (ci.yml:101,131,153,168,283,321), buildx (ci.yml:253, docker.yml:20), build-push (ci.yml:255, docker.yml:41,63), upload/download-artifact (ci.yml:330, security.yml:39, release.yml:118,124,139), login/metadata (docker.yml:24,32,54), mdbook/pages trio (pages.yml:51,84,87,104) and gh-release (security.yml:62, release.yml:151) are all SHA-pinned. Policy is inconsistent; checkout executes first in every job with repo write-adjacent context, and dtolnay/rust-toolchain is third-party.
findings.root_cause: Actions were migrated to SHA-pinning incrementally (v1.12-era work); checkout and rust-toolchain kept trailing '# v4'/'# v1' comments that mimic pin annotations without providing pinning.
findings.impact: A compromised or force-pushed mutable tag on actions/checkout or dtolnay/rust-toolchain flows into every CI, release, docker, pages and security workflow automatically; runner code execution + toolchain substitution = supply-chain RCE vector into the build that ships release binaries (release.yml).
findings.recommendation: SHA-pin all 30 references. Dependabot (dependabot.yml:20-25) already tracks github-actions, so pin via its pinning PRs or git ls-remote, keeping the version comment.

fix_examples.before:
- uses: actions/checkout@v4 # v4
- uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@v1
  with:
    toolchain: 1.95.0
fix_examples.after:
- uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
- uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@<40-hex-sha-of-v1> # v1 (git ls-remote https://github.com/dtolnay/rust-toolchain v1)
  with:
    toolchain: 1.95.0

findings.fix_guide: For each workflow, run git ls-remote https://github.com/actions/checkout v4 and https://github.com/dtolnay/rust-toolchain v1, replace tag with full SHA, retain comment. Verify with the detection query until it returns zero rows. Dependabot will then propose SHA bumps with inline diffs.

effort_estimate.breakdown: resolve 2 SHAs (5) + edit 30 refs across 6 files (35) + verify via grep (10) + wait for green CI (10)

detection_method.query: uses:\s*\S+@v\d with negative match on 40-hex SHA

confidence.rationale: Direct read of all 6 workflow files; every occurrence enumerated by grep; SHA-pinned vs not verified line-by-line.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Pure textual fact; no convention documents mutable-tag pinning as intentional. Trailing '# v4' comments show pin intent, not a documented exception.

findings.title: No concurrency group / cancel-in-progress in ci.yml (only pages.yml has one)
findings.description: ci.yml triggers on every push to any PR branch targeting main plus pushes to main (lines 3-7) and runs a 73-crate clippy, 3-OS test matrix, two release-mode CLI builds, docker build and the equivalence harness. No workflow-level concurrency block exists (grep '^concurrency:' matches only pages.yml:19-21). security.yml (push+weekly cron lines 3-10) and bufflings.yml also lack it. Only test-framework has timeout-minutes:25 (ci.yml:146); all other jobs ride the 360-minute default.
findings.root_cause: Concurrency was added to pages.yml (deploy-safe pattern already in-repo at pages.yml:19-21) but never propagated to the compute-heavy CI workflow.
findings.impact: Superseded commits on rapidly-updated PR branches keep burning full matrix runs (ubuntu+windows+macOS); stale runs interleave with the Monday security cron; wasted Actions minutes and delayed feedback; a hung job without timeout-minutes stalls to 6h.
findings.recommendation: Add workflow-level concurrency keyed on ref, cancel-in-progress for PRs only (keep main runs cancellable too); add timeout-minutes to the long jobs (clippy, test-core, self-host, equivalence).

findings.fix_guide: Insert the block after the on: section (line 7) in ci.yml; optionally mirror in security.yml with cancel-in-progress: false for the scheduled run. Add timeout-minutes: 30-60 to clippy/test-core/self-host/equivalence jobs.

confidence.rationale: Absence verified by grep over all workflows and full ci.yml read; pages.yml precedent proves the team pattern.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: No doc states CI concurrency is intentionally omitted; AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md are silent on it.

findings.title: Zero CI for editors/vscode and actions/setup-buff; dependabot lacks npm ecosystem
findings.description: No workflow references vscode, npm or node (grep across .github/workflows/*.yml returns 0 matches). editors/vscode/package.json (229 lines) defines a real build ('compile': tsc -p ./, line 215) and runtime dep vscode-languageclient ^9.0.1 (line 221) â€” the shipped extension (buff-vscode-1.3.0 per its AGENTS.md) is never compile-verified. actions/setup-buff is a published TS GitHub Action with committed dist/index.js and jest suites (__tests__/) that never run in CI. dependabot.yml (lines 2-25) covers only cargo + github-actions ecosystems â€” npm deps in both packages are never updated.
findings.root_cause: TS/npm assets were shipped (T118, T139-era setup-buff) without a companion CI job; dependabot config was authored only for the Rust workspace.
findings.impact: Extension and action compile breakage ships undetected to users; setup-buff src/ can drift from committed dist/index.js (supply-chain surface consumers pin); npm deps (incl. vscode-languageclient) receive zero security updates â€” known JS advisories never gated.
findings.recommendation: Add a workflow job: setup-node + npm ci + npm run compile in editors/vscode, and npm ci + npx jest in actions/setup-buff; add an npm ecosystem entry to dependabot.yml for both directories.

fix_examples.after:
jobs:
  vscode-extension:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@<sha> # v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: editors/vscode/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
        working-directory: editors/vscode
      - run: npm run compile
        working-directory: editors/vscode

  cargo-deny:

findings.fix_guide: 1) New job in ci.yml (or dedicated workflow) compiling editors/vscode; 2) second job running jest in actions/setup-buff; 3) append to .github/dependabot.yml: '- package-ecosystem: npm, directory: /editors/vscode' and same for /actions/setup-buff. Note: editors/vscode/AGENTS.md documents a MANUAL QA checklist â€” automated compile+test is complementary, not duplicate.

effort_estimate.breakdown: author jobs (40) + dependabot entries (5) + fix whatever compile errors surface (45)

detection_method.query: vscode|npm|node in .github/workflows/*.yml (0 matches); package-ecosystem: in dependabot.yml

confidence.rationale: Absence triple-verified (workflow grep, dependabot read, glob of editors/vscode). Partial FP risk: manual QA is documented, but no automated gate exists.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: editors/vscode/AGENTS.md + README document 'manual QA checklist' and rationale for no e2e tests â€” documented intent exists; however compile-level CI and npm dependabot are absent and undocumented as intentional.

findings.title: Release artifacts unsigned â€” checksums and SBOM only, no cosign/GPG signature
findings.description: release.yml is tag-triggered (lines 21-24) and publishes 5 archives + .sha256 sidecars (checksums at lines 106-115, publish at 150-160) with no signing step (grep cosign|gpg|minisign|sign across release.yml/security.yml: only 'release' name matches). SBOM does exist but cross-workflow: security.yml:47-64 generates cyclonedx.json on v* tag push and attaches it. Homebrew/scoop installers verify embedded sha256 (ci.yml installer-lint) but nothing cryptographically binds artifacts to the repo identity.
findings.root_cause: T58 release work shipped checksums + SBOM; signing was never added to the runbook (docs/RELEASE.md not cited for signing).
findings.impact: Installers and buffup (crates/buffup downloads from GitHub Releases into ~/.buff) rely on GitHub integrity alone; a compromised release asset or registry mirror cannot be detected by clients â€” authenticity gap for a toolchain that installs native binaries.
findings.recommendation: Add keyless cosign signing (sign-blob) of archives + sha256 sidecars in the release job; publish .sig/.crt alongside, and document verification in docs/RELEASE.md and the book install chapter.

fix_examples.before:
- name: Create GitHub Release with artifacts
  uses: softprops/action-gh-release@3bb12739c298aeb8a4eeaf626c5b8d85266b0e65 # v2
fix_examples.after:
- uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@<sha> # v3
- name: Sign release artifacts (keyless)
  run: |
    for f in artifacts/*.tar.gz artifacts/*.zip artifacts/*.sha256; do
      cosign sign-blob --yes --output-signature "$f.sig" "$f"
    done
- name: Create GitHub Release with artifacts
  uses: softprops/action-gh-release@3bb12739c298aeb8a4eeaf626c5b8d85266b0e65 # v2
  with:
    files: |
      artifacts/*.tar.gz
      artifacts/*.zip
      artifacts/*.sha256
      artifacts/*.sig

findings.fix_guide: Add cosign-installer step before publish; sign-blob each archive and checksum (keyless, no secrets needed; workflow already has id-token? release.yml lacks id-token: write â€” add it to the release job permissions alongside contents:write at line 134). Test on a v-test tag.

effort_estimate.breakdown: workflow changes (30) + permissions tweak (5) + end-to-end tag test (60) + docs (25)

confidence.rationale: Full read of release.yml (160 lines) shows checksums+publish only; SBOM located in security.yml; no signing primitive anywhere.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Not claimed absent as defect of scope docs; checksums/SBOM existence credited. README/docs/RELEASE.md runbook may plan signing â€” not checked (docs/RELEASE.md unread), hence confidence 0.95 not 0.99.

findings.title: Unpinned cargo install of gate tools cargo-audit and cargo-cyclonedx
findings.description: security.yml:27 'cargo install cargo-audit --locked' and :58 'cargo install cargo-cyclonedx --locked' install latest at run time â€” no --version pin, no cache (fresh source compile each run). The hard gate's tool itself floats. Contrast: pages.yml:44-48 pins wasm-bindgen-cli to the exact resolved version via cargo tree extraction. Ignore-list source of truth .cargo/audit.toml (25 RUSTSEC IDs, lines 12-73) is good; gate is continue-on-error: false (line 36) per CONTRIBUTING.md:95.
findings.root_cause: Official cargo-audit docs recommend bare 'cargo install cargo-audit --locked'; copied without adding version pinning or rust-cache.
findings.impact: A new cargo-audit major release can change advisory matching/ignore semantics mid-week and flip the gate (false red or false green â€” e.g. ignore-format changes silently bypassing .cargo/audit.toml entries); releases are also skipped by the audit job on tag pushes (security.yml:19 condition), so the floating tool gates main but not release artifacts.
findings.recommendation: Pin both tools with --version <x.y.z> (bump deliberately via dependabot/renovate), and add Swatinem/rust-cache or cargo-install cache to cut the multi-minute source build per run.

fix_examples.before:
- name: Install cargo-audit
  run: cargo install cargo-audit --locked
fix_examples.after:
- name: Install cargo-audit (pinned)
  run: cargo install cargo-audit --locked --version 0.21.2

findings.fix_guide: Choose current stable versions, add --version to both installs (lines 27, 58), add rust-cache step keyed 'cargo-audit' after checkout, and record the pin rationale in the existing comment block (lines 29-34).

effort_estimate.breakdown: pick versions (5) + edit (5) + trigger workflow_dispatch run to validate (10)

confidence.rationale: Direct read; unpinned installs are textual facts; severity judgment (gate-tool drift) is standard supply-chain practice.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: No repo doc states floating gate tools are intentional; ignore-list location fact (prior squad) independently verified at .cargo/audit.toml.

findings.title: $SKIPPED vs $SKIP echo bug in buff-validation golden harness summary line
findings.description: ci.yml:187 initializes 'PASS=0; SKIP=0; FAIL=0' and :203 increments $SKIP, but the summary at :207 echoes '$SKIPPED' â€” an unset variable that expands to empty under bash (no set -u in the step), producing 'Results: N passed, N failed,  skipped'. Verified exactly as reported by prior squad. The actual gate is sound: FAIL>0 triggers ::error:: + exit 1 (lines 208-211), so severity is cosmetic/log-accuracy only.
findings.root_cause: Variable renamed SKIP during the v1.39 golden-harness introduction; the summary echo kept the old name.
findings.impact: Skipped count (buff run failures on forward-declared examples, line 202) is never visible in the step summary â€” mildly misleading harness reporting for maintainers tracking the skip backlog.
findings.fix_guide: Edit line 207; optionally add 'set -u' at the top of the run block (line 185) so future unset-variable typos fail loudly instead of printing empty.

confidence.rationale: Line-exact verification of declaration (187), increment (203) and echo (207); bash unset-expansion semantics are well-defined.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Pure textual fact; no FP scenario â€” the gate itself was checked and is NOT silently passing (exit 1 at line 210).

findings.title: No container image scanning; slim.Dockerfile never built outside tag pushes
findings.description: docker.yml (72 lines, tag-triggered) builds and pushes builder+slim multi-arch images (lines 40-50, 62-72) with no trivy/grype/scan step anywhere. ci.yml docker-build (248-262) validates ONLY docker/builder.Dockerfile on PRs â€” docker/slim.Dockerfile is first compiled at release time. Positives verified: secrets DOCKER_USERNAME/DOCKER_PASSWORD used only via login-action gated 'if: github.event_name != pull_request' (lines 23-28) with no exposure into build args; base images are digest-pinned (builder.Dockerfile:12,31; slim.Dockerfile:12).
findings.root_cause: T61-era multi-arch docker work shipped build+push without a scanning stage; ci.yml's PR validation predates the slim image.
findings.impact: A CVE-carrying image (e.g. in the rust toolchain layer baked into builder) is published to Docker Hub on every tag with no detection; a broken slim.Dockerfile is discovered only during a release, blocking the tag.
findings.recommendation: Add aquasecurity/trivy-action after each build-push scanning the pushed tags (exit-code 1 on CRITICAL/HIGH, or report-only initially); add a slim.Dockerfile build (push: false) to ci.yml docker-build job.

fix_examples.before:
- name: Build and push (builder)
        uses: docker/build-push-action@ca052bb54ab0790a636c9b5f226502c73d547a25 # v5
        with: ...
fix_examples.after:
- name: Build and push (builder)
        uses: docker/build-push-action@ca052bb54ab0790a636c9b5f226502c73d547a25 # v5
        with: ...
      - name: Scan builder image
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@<sha>
        with:
          image-ref: 'buff:latest-builder'
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
          exit-code: '1'

findings.fix_guide: 1) Append trivy steps after lines 50 and 72 in docker.yml (SHA-pin the action per AUD-CICD-001 policy); 2) in ci.yml docker-build add a second build-push step for docker/slim.Dockerfile with push: false. Decide gate-vs-report posture and document in the job comment.

effort_estimate.breakdown: add scan steps (15) + slim PR build (10) + triage initial findings (20)

detection_method.query: trivy|grype|scan in docker.yml (0 matches); slim.Dockerfile in ci.yml (0 matches)

confidence.rationale: Full docker.yml read + ci.yml read; absence-based finding, partially mitigated by digest-pinned bases (credited inline).

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: No doc claims scanning is deferred; AGENTS.md documents docker gates without mentioning scan decisions.

findings.title: self-host-check header comment falsely claims HARD GATE while job is count-only
findings.description: ci.yml:264 comment reads 'P0.2: The 7 baseline files below MUST pass buff check for any PR to merge' under a 'HARD GATE' banner (line 264 comment block 264-274), but the job (275-305) never exits nonzero â€” failures only echo 'FAIL: $f' (line 301) and the run ends with a ::notice:: count (line 304). AGENTS.md NOTES and CONTRIBUTING.md:104 both document the job as intentionally count-only. The in-file comment contradicts both and promises a merge gate that does not exist.
findings.root_cause: Comment written when self-host was planned as a hard gate (P0.2); behavior was relaxed to count-only but the header comment was never updated.
findings.impact: Maintainers trusting the workflow header will believe self-host regressions block merges â€” a documented-vs-actual gate mismatch that can hide corpus regressions during review.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the comment block to state count-only semantics and link CONTRIBUTING.md advisory table; optionally emit FAIL count as a job summary.
